t.5.43.1: Then, urged on by the lord of the Rākṣasas, those seven sons of the minister, blazing with the splendour of fire, went forth from that palace.
t.5.43.2: Attended by a mighty force, bearing bows and possessed of great strength, accomplished in arms and foremost among those skilled in weapons, they were each eager to outdo one another in winning victory.
t.5.43.4: Those warriors of boundless valour, thrilled with delight, twanged their bows adorned with refined gold, and they looked like rain-clouds flashing with lightning.
t.5.43.3: With great chariots yoked with horses, covered with nets of gold, bearing flagstaffs and banners, and rumbling with a roar like the thunder of rain-clouds.
t.5.43.5: Then the mothers of those servants, learning that the Kiṃkaras had been slain, were overwhelmed and bewildered with grief, together with their kinsmen and friends.
t.5.43.7: Releasing a rain of arrows, those bulls among the Nairṛtas, the roar of their chariots like thunder, moved about like rain-laden clouds pouring down showers.
t.5.43.6: Vying with one another and adorned with ornaments of refined gold, they rushed upon Hanumān, who stood firmly upon the archway.
t.5.43.8: Then Hanumān, showered by those torrents of arrows, had his form completely covered, like the king of mountains veiled by rains.
t.5.43.9: That swift-moving monkey, ranging through the clear sky, evaded the arrows of those heroes and the rushing onsets of their chariots.
t.5.43.10: Sporting in the sky with those bow-bearing warriors, the hero shone forth, just as the mighty Wind, lord in the heavens, shines amid clouds that bear the rainbow.
t.5.43.11: Raising a terrible roar and terrifying that great army, the mighty Hanumān hurled himself with great speed upon those rākṣasas.
t.5.43.12: That scorcher of foes struck some with his palm and some with his feet; some he smote with his fist, and some he tore apart with his nails.
t.5.43.13: The monkey crushed some with his chest and others with his thighs; some, at his roar alone, fell to the ground right there.
t.5.43.14: Then, when they had been struck down and had fallen to the ground, that entire army, tormented by fear, fled in all ten directions.
t.5.43.16: Having slain those mighty rākṣasas, the monkey of great strength and fierce valour, that hero eager to fight yet again with other rākṣasas, went back to that very archway.
t.5.43.15: The elephants trumpeted in discordant cries, the horses fell to the ground, and the earth was strewn with chariots whose seats, banners and parasols lay shattered.
